controls.label: Workflow-level concurrency
controls.syntax:
concurrency:
  group: repo-care-${{ github.repository }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
  queue: max
controls.purpose: Prevents overlapping runs for the chosen repository, branch, issue, pull request, or custom context.

controls.label: Engine-level concurrency
controls.syntax:
engine:
  id: copilot
  concurrency:
    group: gh-aw-copilot-${{ github.repository }}
    queue: max
controls.purpose: Serializes scarce or expensive agent execution independently from workflow-level grouping.

controls.label: Safe-output concurrency
controls.purpose: Serializes application of issues, pull requests, or other writes so independent agent runs do not race.
controls.behavior: The safe-output group uses cancel-in-progress false so queued writes wait rather than cancel.

controls.label: Queue preservation
controls.purpose: Preserves all pending runs in arrival order instead of retaining only the latest pending run.
controls.caveat: Use only when every queued run remains valuable; otherwise skip, batch, or deduplicate before inference.

controls.label: Fan-out job discriminator
controls.scope: Compiler-generated agent, output, and conclusion job groups
controls.purpose: Appends a unique expression so intentional fan-out runs do not cancel or block one another at generated job-level groups.
controls.caveat: It preserves fan-out; it is not a rate limit and can increase simultaneous work.

controls.label: Conclusion concurrency
controls.purpose: Ensures reporting, cleanup, and outcome summaries complete in order without colliding.
controls.caveat: Generated automatically; configure a job discriminator only when separate fan-out conclusion lanes are required.

controls.label: Per-user rate limit
controls.scope: Pre-activation starts by actor and event window
controls.syntax:
user-rate-limit:
  max-runs-per-window: 3
  window: 60
  events: [workflow_dispatch, issue_comment]
  ignored-roles: []
controls.purpose: Limits how frequently one user can trigger selected workflow events.
controls.distinction: Rate limiting controls admission over time. Concurrency controls overlap and queue behavior after admission. Use both for event-storm protection.

selectionGuide.situation: Repeated updates to one issue or pull request
A shared provider or model must not run many agents at once
Multiple runs may create duplicate or conflicting repository writes
selectionGuide.control: Use safe-output concurrency plus deduplication and operation maximums.

selectionGuide.situation: Every fan-out worker must complete independently
selectionGuide.control: Use job-discriminator, then add an explicit capacity or rate policy.

selectionGuide.situation: One actor can generate too many admitted runs
selectionGuide.control: Use user-rate-limit; concurrency alone only creates a longer queue.
